# The step of a dot product of two limbs, on arrays of the program: the product and the sum of the guarded elements

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `dot_entry_step_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $t$ of $s + x y$:

$$t \approx s + x y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $s = s_0 + s_1$, $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $t = t_0 + t_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dot(x, y)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 2>>` | the step of the loop the function calls, once per element; not `constexpr`; rounds; in the lane order of the build, or, with `kairn::sequential`, in the sequential order (loop `dot_2_entry`; every limb of each factor guarded, rule R3 on the factors of a fused operation) |
| `dot(sequential, x, y)` | `Sequential`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 2>>` |  |
| `conv(x, y, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | `bool` | each coefficient a sequential `dot_2_entry` (loop `conv_2_entry`; every limb of each factor guarded) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the functions are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/batch.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include; a view of `T` is taken where the table writes a view of `const T`. They take no marker: a function on arrays compiles only while the kernels of its loop are proved ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $s$ is normalized: $s_0 = \mathrm{RN}(s_0 + s_1)$.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t$ is normalized: $t_0 = \mathrm{RN}(t_0 + t_1)$.
- $\lvert t - (s + x y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 4u u)}{1 - 4u} + 4\right) u^2\,(\lvert s\rvert + \lvert x y\rvert) + 2\,\eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $\approx 8.6282 \times 10^{-32}$ | $\approx 2.4869 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1073} \approx 9.8813 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-148} \approx 2.8026 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.c000000000002p-104`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.c00004p-46f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `dot_entry_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/StepKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/StepKernels.v), against `dot_entry_step_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions dot_entry_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition dot_entry_step_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (4 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s0 s1 x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec s0 s1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let '(t0, t1) := dot_entry_step_2 emin prec tie_even s0 s1 x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  normalized_2 emin prec t0 t1 /\
  Rabs ((t0 + t1) - ((s0 + s1) + ((x0 + x1) * (y0 + y1)))) <= (((3 * (1 + ((4 * u prec) * u prec))) / (1 - (4 * u prec))) + 4) * u prec ^ 2 * (Rabs (s0 + s1) + Rabs ((x0 + x1) * (y0 + y1))) + 2 * eta emin.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `dot_entry_step_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** dot_step_2 on the guarded limbs of the elements (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation); bounds from [MR22](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#mr22). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/dot_entry_step_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/dot_entry_step_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`dot_step_2`](dot_step_2.md).

```
# The step of dot_2_entry, the dot product of two limbs of arrays the program supplies: dot_step_2,
# p = mul_2_2(x, y); s = add_2_2(s, p), on the limbs of the elements guarded (rule R3, the factors
# of a fused operation: architecture.md). dot_step_2 only multiplies its elements, which R3 alone
# does not guard; but mul_2_2 takes them as factors of fused operations whose addends are not zero,
# and a compiler that sees the other factor to be 1 rewrites fma(x, 1, s) as x + s and may fuse a
# product the program stored into the array into that addition (seen in the dot product of one
# limb, not measured in this one). After the guards each limb is a number of the format, the
# rounded product at most. Its claims are those of dot_step_2: the guard is the identity on numbers
# of the format.

gx0      = guard(x0)
gx1      = guard(x1)
gy0      = guard(y0)
gy1      = guard(y1)
(t0, t1) = dot_step_2(s0, s1, gx0, gx1, gy0, gy1)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#dot_entry_step_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
